title: DNA: Paired Helix
explanation: Two smooth sugar-phosphate backbones wind around paired connectors. Complementary bases pair across the strands; representative colors distinguish partners, not a real sequence. Schematic, not to molecular scale.

parts.name: Left sugar-phosphate backbone
parts.detail: One continuous backbone winds around the shared axis; its teal color identifies this schematic strand.

parts.name: Right sugar-phosphate backbone
parts.detail: A matching continuous backbone, half a turn out of phase with the teal strand.

parts.name: First half of base-pair connectors
parts.detail: Evenly samples both backbone paths; each short segment runs from the teal backbone to the midpoint of a connector. Pale cream is a representative base color.

parts.name: Second half of base-pair connectors
parts.detail: Completes each sampled connector from its midpoint to the amber backbone. Coral distinguishes the representative complementary partner; no sequence is depicted.

steps.title: Trace the backbones
steps.explanation: Follow each smooth strand around the shared axis. Their half-turn offset gives the paired helix its twisted ladder form.

steps.title: Inspect complementary pairing
steps.explanation: Look along a few connectors: cream and coral halves meet midway between the backbones. The contrasting colors suggest complementary base partners, not an actual sequence.

steps.title: Separate the backbones
steps.explanation: First the connectors disappear; then the backbones spread apart. Compare the intact paired arrangement with separated strands—the connectors are not attached in this view.

experiment.label: Backbone spacing
experiment.lowExplanation: The strands share the paired helix arrangement, with complementary connector halves bridging between them.
experiment.highExplanation: As spacing increases, connectors are hidden before the backbones move apart; this illustrates strand separation, not a molecular process.
